# WhatsApp Agent

Link a WhatsApp number by scanning a QR code, and every **incoming** message is saved: photos, videos, voice notes and documents go to a linked **Google Drive**, message text stays in a small local log, and a web page lets you browse both. An optional auto-reply bot can answer messages (`bot-config.json`).

```
archive/                    # created on first run, never committed
  <sessionId>/
    <chatId>/
      messages.jsonl        # one JSON record per message (text, stays local)
      media/                # outbox: files wait here only until Drive has them
```

## Setup (first time)

Works on **macOS, Windows and Linux**. Needs **Node 22 LTS** (check with `node -v`) and git.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:junaid-appointy/whatsapp-agent.git
cd whatsapp-agent
npm install        # also installs this app; first time takes a few minutes (downloads Chrome)
```

Create the settings file from the example, then open it and fill in `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (see "Google Drive" below):

```bash
# macOS / Linux
cp apps/whatsapp-agent/.env.example apps/whatsapp-agent/.env

# Windows (Command Prompt or PowerShell)
copy apps\whatsapp-agent\.env.example apps\whatsapp-agent\.env
```

**The bot only replies when called.** A message has to start with the trigger word (`"trigger": "bot"` in `bot-config.json`, e.g. *"bot what time is the meeting?"*). Every other message is just saved, and the AI is never called for it. Set `"enabled": false` to turn replies off completely, or `"requireTrigger": false` to answer every direct message.

## Run

```bash
npm run whatsapp-agent
```

Everything happens in the terminal:

1. **WhatsApp.** A QR code is printed. On the phone: WhatsApp > Settings > Linked devices > Link a device, and scan it. A saved login reconnects by itself, with no scan (also after a restart).
2. **Google Drive.** Once WhatsApp is linked, a Google sign-in link is printed. Open it on **any** computer or phone and allow access. The browser then lands on a `localhost` address that doesn't load: copy that whole address, paste it into the terminal and press Enter. (If you signed in on the same computer, it connects by itself.)

Type `help` in the terminal for commands: `status`, `qr` (fresh code), `drive` (new sign-in link), `drive off`, `retry`, `unlink`. The web page at http://localhost:4100 still works too (browse and search the archive, same buttons).

The command starts OpenWA and the agent together, keeps the computer from sleeping while it runs (macOS `caffeinate`, Windows power request, Linux `systemd-inhibit`), and restarts either one if it crashes (up to 5 times). OpenWA only shows warnings and errors; set `LOG_LEVEL=info` to see its full log. `Ctrl+C` stops everything. Your WhatsApp login, database and archive are created on your machine on first run (`data/`, `apps/whatsapp-agent/archive/`) and are never committed.

### Keeping a laptop running

- Keep it **plugged in**. Idle sleep is blocked while running, but **closing the lid still sleeps** the laptop.
  - macOS: keep the lid open (or use an external display).
  - Windows: Control Panel → Power Options → *Choose what closing the lid does* → **Do nothing** (when plugged in).
- Windows may ask whether Node.js can use the network the first time. Choose **Private networks** and allow.

## Finding files: references and tags

- **Reference.** Every message gets a short permanent id like `WA-260925-7K3FQ2` (date + 6 characters, no look-alike letters). It's shown under each file, starts the file's name in Drive, and `http://localhost:4100/f/WA-260925-7K3FQ2` always opens that file (from Drive once uploaded).
- **Tags.** Put `#hashtags` in the caption when sending, e.g. *"#asset23 screen cracked #repair"*. Tags ignore case and punctuation, so `#Asset-23`, `#asset_23` and `#ASSET23` are all `asset23`. Hindi and other scripts work too.
- **Search** the page by `#tag`, reference or words, or click any tag. In Drive, search the tag or reference: both are in the file name.
- Each Drive file also carries its details (reference, chat, sender, time, caption, tags) in its description and in Drive `appProperties`, e.g. `appProperties has { key='tag_asset23' and value='1' }` for exact queries.

Files uploaded before this was added keep their old Drive names; they still get a reference and short link on the page.

## Google Drive

Press **Connect Google Drive**, sign in with any Google account, and every photo, video, voice note and document goes to a `WhatsApp Archive/<chat name>/` folder in that Drive.

Each file is written to `media/` first and **deleted once Drive confirms the upload**, so the laptop holds nothing long term. If Drive or the network is down, or no Drive is connected yet, files wait in `media/` and go up later; nothing is lost. The UI streams already uploaded media back from Drive. Uploads are tracked in `archive/.drive-uploads.jsonl`, so nothing is uploaded twice. Set `KEEP_LOCAL_MEDIA=1` to keep local copies as well.

The app only asks for the `drive.file` permission: it can see the files it creates and nothing else in the Drive.

One-time setup in Google Cloud Console (free):

1. Create a project, enable the **Google Drive API**.
2. **OAuth consent screen** → User type **External** (so any Google account, not just your Workspace, can connect). Add the scopes `openid`, `email`, `.../auth/drive.file`.
3. Press **Publish app** (status "In production"). With only these non-sensitive scopes Google needs no review, and sign ins don't expire after 7 days like they do in "Testing".
4. **Credentials** → Create OAuth client ID → **Web application**. Authorized redirect URI: `<PUBLIC_URL>/oauth/google/callback` (default `http://localhost:4100/oauth/google/callback`).
5. Put the client ID and secret in `.env` (see below) and restart.

## Config (env vars)

| Variable         | Default                           | Purpose                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `ARCHIVE_DIR`    | `./archive` next to `server.mjs`  | Where messages and media are written     |
| `ARCHIVER_PORT`  | `4100`                            | UI + webhook port                        |
| `OPENWA_URL`     | `http://127.0.0.1:2785`           | OpenWA API                               |
| `OPENWA_API_KEY` | `dev-admin-key`                   | OpenWA API key (dev default)             |
| `WEBHOOK_URL`    | `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/webhook` | URL OpenWA calls (use an IP, not `localhost`) |
| `WA_SESSION_NAME` | `archiver`                       | Name of the session "Connect WhatsApp" creates |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | none   | Enables the Google Drive button          |
| `PUBLIC_URL`     | `http://localhost:<port>`         | Address people open the UI on; Google redirects back here |
| `DRIVE_FOLDER_NAME` | `WhatsApp Archive`             | Top folder created in Drive              |
| `DRIVE_MEDIA_TYPES` | all media                      | Limit which media go to Drive, e.g. `image/,video/` (others stay local) |
| `KEEP_LOCAL_MEDIA` | off                              | `1` keeps a local copy after upload      |
| `AGENT_CLI`      | on                                | `0` turns off the terminal QR, prompts and commands |

## Limitations

- Only messages received **after** login are captured. There's no history backfill.
- Messages you send from your phone aren't captured, because OpenWA only emits `message.received`.
- In group chats the individual sender isn't in the payload, so only the group is recorded.
- One Google Drive per archiver. Switching to a different Google account only affects new files; ones already uploaded stay in the old Drive (their local copies are gone).
- The UI has no login of its own, so keep it on `127.0.0.1` (the default) or put it behind auth before exposing it. Anyone who can open it can unlink WhatsApp or connect a Drive.

---
name: project-openwa-relay
description: OpenWA (office VPS WhatsApp gateway) findings + recommended pull-relay design for app→WhatsApp curated messages and intake photo proof
metadata:
  type: project
---

Repo is `/Users/appointy/work/OpenWA` (remote `junaid-appointy/whatsapp-agent`), outside the umbrella. Two parts: the OpenWA NestJS gateway (whatsapp-web.js engine, REST on `127.0.0.1:2785`, `X-API-Key`, `POST /api/sessions/:id/messages/send-text|send-image` with `chatId` + `url|base64` + `caption`, groups API) and `apps/whatsapp-agent` (archives INCOMING media to Google Drive with `WA-YYMMDD-XXXXXX` refs + #tags, trigger-word bot, port 4100, `drive.file` scope). Outgoing messages are not archived by the agent.

Analysis given 2026-10-08 (nothing built): recommended a **pull relay** on the VPS (engine on Bifrost cannot reach a localhost gateway, and the OpenWA admin key can unlink/read everything, so never expose it). Engine writes a channel-agnostic notifications outbox from typed inventory events (receipts are idempotent: notify only on fresh insert); relay polls, sends via local OpenWA to an ops group, uploads photo to Drive with the agent's existing drive.mjs, acks with refs; engine keeps the photo only until acked. Dispenses go in a digest, not per event. Field-app photo capture can use the already-installed vision-camera; `expo-file-system` is only a transitive dep of `expo` (not top-level), so whether the dev client links it must be checked on device before promising "no rebuild".

**Why:** user wants app actions posted as curated WhatsApp messages via the office VPS agent, plus intake photo proof. Related: [[project-whatsapp-template-sender]] (Meta Cloud API path stays for visitor-facing messages), [[feedback-automation-surface-readiness]], [[project-ameya-stakeholder]].

Yes, this can work. Your agent already has what's needed: it can send text and photos to any WhatsApp group, and it's already connected to Google Drive. The one thing to design around is which side calls which. I've only analysed it; nothing is built.

## What OpenWA has today

- **The gateway** keeps the WhatsApp login (it drives WhatsApp Web through the `whatsapp-web.js` library). It has a REST API to send text, images, documents and group messages. It listens only on `127.0.0.1:2785` on the VPS, protected by an API key.
- **The agent** saves *incoming* photos and files to Google Drive, gives each a short reference like `WA-261008-7K3FQ2`, supports `#tags`, and has a bot that replies only when called by its trigger word. Messages it *sends* are not saved anywhere.

## The main design problem: who calls whom

The engine runs on Bifrost in the cloud, and the gateway only listens on the VPS itself, so the engine can't reach it. The obvious fix is to put the gateway on the internet. Don't do that: its API key can also unlink WhatsApp and read every chat.

**Recommended: the VPS asks the engine for messages.**

```
field-app ──(normal sync)──▶ engine (Bifrost)
                                │  inventory action happens
                                ▼
                        notification queue (new table, also holds the photo)
                                ▲
              every ~30 s       │  "anything new?"  (one secret, read-only)
                                │
 office VPS:  small relay ──────┘
                │  sends via the local gateway (key never leaves the VPS)
                ▼
          WhatsApp "Office Store" group   +   photo saved to Google Drive (existing Drive code)
                │
                └─▶ relay tells the engine: done, here is the Drive link and message id
```

Why this shape:
- **No open ports on the VPS.** The gateway stays private.
- **Nothing is lost if the VPS or WhatsApp goes down.** Messages wait in the engine and go out once it's back.
- **No duplicate messages.** Receipts in the engine already ignore retries, so the queue only adds a message when a delivery is recorded for the first time.
- **It fits the house rules.** The engine just queues "something happened", with no WhatsApp code in it. The relay is the WhatsApp adapter, and Telegram could later read the same queue.

## Photo proof on receive

1. **Phone:** after counting a delivery, a "Take photo" step uses the camera the scanner already uses. The photo is saved at about 1280 px, roughly 200–300 KB. Offline, it waits in the sync queue like every other write.
2. **Engine:** stores the photo only until the VPS confirms it was sent, then deletes it and keeps the Drive link and reference on the receipt. Storing photos permanently in Postgres would fill the free 500 MB in about a year.
3. **VPS:** posts it to the group, for example:
   > 📦 **Received** · Sugar 5 kg × 2 packs, exp 20 Nov
   > By Sana · Store A · 4:12 pm · Ref WA-261008-7K3FQ2

   It also uploads the photo to `Drive/WhatsApp Archive/Inventory/` with `#receipt #sugar` tags, so it shows up in the agent's existing search.

## What to post, so the group doesn't turn into noise

| Event | When | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery received (with photo) | Right away | This is the proof |
| Count corrected with a difference | Right away | Possible loss, someone should look |
| Low stock / out of stock | Right away, at most once per item per day | Action needed |
| Take outs | One summary per day (e.g. 6 pm) | Per-item messages would flood the group |
| Visitor check-ins, staff in/out | Later, same pipe | Opt-in per group |

Each message type has its own on/off switch and target group in settings. That also leaves room to run these from the automation editor later.

## Cost

- **Monthly: ₹0.** The VPS already runs. Google Drive's free 15 GB holds years of 250 KB photos. WhatsApp through the gateway has no per-message fee.
- **One-time:** the build, roughly 3–4 days (below).
- **Cheaper non-tech option:** the storekeeper photographs the delivery and posts it to the group by hand. That gives no link to the receipt, no search and no daily summary, and in practice people stop doing it within weeks.

## Risks to say out loud

1. **Number ban.** whatsapp-web.js is unofficial, so WhatsApp can ban an automated number. Use a dedicated SIM, send only to your own internal groups, and keep volume low (a few dozen messages a day is fine). Never use it for visitors. Visitor messages stay on the official Meta API, which the engine already uses.
2. **Breakage on WhatsApp Web updates.** whatsapp-web.js sometimes breaks when WhatsApp updates its web app. Messages then pile up in the engine until the library is updated. Nothing is lost, but nothing goes out either. The relay should show "WhatsApp offline since…" somewhere visible.
3. **App rebuild unknown.** The file-saving module the photo step needs comes bundled inside Expo, not listed directly in the app. I need to check on your phone whether the current dev app already includes it. If not, it's one rebuild.
4. **The VPS must stay up.** The agent was written for a laptop (it blocks sleep). On a VPS it should run as a service that restarts on its own.

## Build order

1. **Engine (about 1 day):** notification queue table, typed events from receipt / correction / low stock, two relay endpoints (fetch new, mark done) behind one secret, and the daily take-out summary.
2. **VPS relay (about 1 day):** a small module inside the agent that checks the queue, sends through the local gateway, uploads to Drive with tags and confirms back. Settings for which group gets which event.
3. **App photo step (1 to 1.5 days):** camera step on Receive, photo held in the sync queue, upload with retry, and a "Photo sent" mark on the receipt.
4. **Later:** the Supabase port gets the same two endpoints. Optionally, an AI check of "photo vs counted amount", once a working Gemini key exists (the current one is rejected).

To plan the build I need four answers from you:
- Which WhatsApp group (or groups) should get the messages?
- Should the delivery photo be **required** or **optional**?
- Is the dispense summary once a day enough?
- Is the bot number on a dedicated SIM?

cd /Users/appointy/work/OfficeOperationsUmbrella/office-ops-engine/src/mastra; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='lib/postgres-schema.ts'
s=open(p).read()
old="""    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_whatsapp_messages_recipient ON whatsapp_messages(recipient);
  `;
}"""
assert s.count(old)==1
new="""    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_whatsapp_messages_recipient ON whatsapp_messages(recipient);

    -- A delivery groups the receipts counted together (one standalone
    -- receive, or one order session) and carries one proof photo.
    ALTER TABLE inventory_receipts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS delivery_id TEXT;
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_inv_receipts_delivery
      ON inventory_receipts(delivery_id) WHERE delivery_id IS NOT NULL;

    -- Delivery proof photos. The bytes are held only until the ops relay
    -- confirms the photo was posted (and archived to Drive on the VPS);
    -- then they are dropped and proof_ref (the archive reference) stays.
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS inventory_delivery_photos (
      delivery_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      site_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      receipt_ids TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
      mime TEXT NOT NULL,
      bytes BYTEA,
      size_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
      guard_id TEXT,
      guard_name TEXT,
      taken_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
      proof_ref TEXT,
      posted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );

    -- Outgoing ops messages, channel-agnostic (core/ops-outbox.ts). A relay
    -- (today: the WhatsApp agent on the office VPS) claims, posts and acks
    -- them. dedupe_key makes every producer safe to call twice.
    -- status: waiting (needs more data, e.g. receipts still syncing),
    -- pending, sending (claimed), sent, failed, skipped.
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ops_notifications (
      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      site_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      kind TEXT NOT NULL,
      dedupe_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      subject_id TEXT,
      payload JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
      status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
      attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
      last_error TEXT,
      claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
      sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
      delivery JSONB,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ops_notifications_open
      ON ops_notifications(status, created_at) WHERE status IN ('waiting', 'pending', 'sending');
  `;
}"""
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
echo ok

echo "== wrong secret (expect 401)"

echo "== correction with difference + low stock (set threshold first)"
psql -h /tmp/rbacpg -p 55432 -U postgres -q -c "update appointy_ops.inventory_stock set threshold=3 where barcode='8901262150212'"
curl -s "${H[@]}" -X POST $B/api/inventory/corrections -d "{\"id\":\"crn_$R\",\"barcode\":\"8901262150212\",\"product_name\":\"Milk\",\"old_qty\":6.4,\"new_qty\":2.5,\"lots\":[{\"expiry_date\":null,\"qty\":2.5}]}"; echo
sleep 1
echo "== take outs today + digest row"
curl -s "${H[@]}" -X POST $B/api/inventory/issues -d "{\"id\":\"dsp_$R\",\"barcode\":\"8901725133979\",\"product_name\":\"Sugar\",\"qty\":0.05,\"taken_by\":\"Sana\",\"dispense_qty\":250,\"dispense_unit\":\"g\"}"; echo
psql -h /tmp/rbacpg -p 55432 -U postgres -q -c "insert into appointy_ops.ops_notifications (id, site_id, kind, dedupe_key, subject_id) values ('opn_digest$R','site-dev','inventory.daily_takeouts','test-digest-$R', to_char(now() at time zone 'Asia/Kolkata','YYYY-MM-DD')) on conflict do nothing"
echo "== claim (expect correction, low stock, digest)"
OUT=$(curl -s -H "x-relay-secret: $S" -X POST $B/api/ops-relay/claim -d '{"limit":20}')
echo "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(m["kind"],"\n"+m["text"]+"\n") for m in d["messages"]]'
echo "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(" ".join(m["id"] for m in d["messages"]))' > /tmp/rbacpg/claimed.txt
echo "== fail one (expect back to pending)"
FIRST=$(cut -d' ' -f1 /tmp/rbacpg/claimed.txt)
curl -s -H "x-relay-secret: $S" -X POST $B/api/ops-relay/ack -d "{\"id\":\"$FIRST\",\"ok\":false,\"error\":\"WhatsApp offline\"}"; echo
psql -h /tmp/rbacpg -p 55432 -U postgres -At -c "select kind, status, attempts, coalesce(last_error,'') from appointy_ops.ops_notifications order by created_at desc limit 6"
EOF

content.text:
Your usage limit has been reached, so I'm stopping here. The WhatsApp integration is built and works on my machine, but no real WhatsApp message has been sent yet and nothing is committed or deployed. I tested with a local test database and a fake WhatsApp gateway, so neither your live WhatsApp login nor real data was touched.

**What's built**
- **Engine (`office-ops-engine`):** a message queue for the ops group, three endpoints the VPS relay uses (fetch new messages, fetch a photo, report back) behind one shared secret, the delivery photo upload, and the messages themselves:
  - 📦 Delivery received, with the photo, every item and its expiry, and who received it.
  - ✏️ Count corrected, e.g. "App had 6 l 400 ml, shelf has 2 l 500 ml".
  - ⚠️ Running low and 🚫 out of stock, at most once a day per item.
  - 📋 Taken out today, sent once after 6 pm.
- **Behaviour I verified:**
  - A delivery's message waits until all its items have synced.
  - A repeated upload never sends a message twice.
  - A failed send is retried.
  - Once a photo is posted, its copy is deleted from the database and only the archive reference is kept.
  - Nothing is queued until the relay is set up.
  - Messages older than a day are skipped instead of posted late. Delivery proofs are kept for a week.
- **Supabase port:** the same changes plus migration `0013_ops_relay.sql`. It produced the same results on the same test. The RBAC tests still pass 22/22 on both backends. The port's inventory tests are at 62/63; the one failure is the old timing-sensitive test, not this work.
- **WhatsApp agent (`OpenWA`):** a new `relay.mjs` that checks the engine every 30 seconds, finds the group by its name, posts each message (photos as images with the caption) and reports back. Every post is filed in the agent's archive with a `WA-…` reference, and the photo goes to Google Drive under the group's folder. The terminal `status` command now shows a relay line.
- **App:**
  - **Finish** on a delivery now opens the camera until a photo is taken, and saving requires it.
  - **Flag and continue** opens the camera too, and the photo saves the delivery.
  - Photos wait on the phone and upload through the sync queue, so they work offline.
  - I added `expo-file-system` pinned to the version already inside your dev app, so no rebuild should be needed.
  - I removed an unused confirm function in the Receive screen that could have saved a delivery without a photo.

**What's left**
1. **Try the camera step on your phone.** Shake the phone and tap **Reload**. The camera and the photo upload have not been tried on a real device yet.
2. **Set up the VPS.** Pull the OpenWA changes, then add these to `apps/whatsapp-agent/.env`:
   - `OPS_RELAY_URL` (the engine's address)
   - `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` (a long random value)
   - `OPS_GROUP` (the test group's name exactly as it shows in WhatsApp)

   If the name doesn't match, the relay prints the groups the bot number is in.
3. **Deploy the engine.** It needs the same `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` set on Bifrost, then a deploy with `--commit`. I'll do this once you tell me to commit and deploy.
4. **Send one real test delivery** and check the group message and the Drive copy.

content.text:
I went through the delivery photo flow again and made it sturdier. The app type-checks, the dev server has the new build, and the local engine is up. I still can't run the camera without a phone, so the photo step itself is untested.

**What I checked or changed:**
- **The phone's file calls** match the library version built into your dev app.
- **Upload order:** the sync queue sends oldest first, so a delivery's items go before its photo. The server handles either order anyway.
- **Saving the photo is sturdier:**
  - It first moves the photo out of the camera's temporary folder, which Android can clear.
  - If moving fails, it copies the photo instead.
  - If that fails too, it keeps the camera's own file, which still uploads unless Android clears it first.

  None of these steps throw away a photo you just took.
- **The "Delivery saved" screen** now shows a camera line: "The photo goes to the office group." It appears after a normal delivery and after "Flag and continue".

**To test on your phone:** shake it and tap **Reload**. Then:
1. Scan an item, add it to the delivery, and go to the delivery list.
2. The main button now reads **Take photo**. Tap it, take the photo, and tap **Use this photo**.
3. The photo shows under the item list and the button changes to **Finish**. Tap it.
4. The "Delivery saved" screen should show the photo line.

Your phone talks to the local engine, which has the relay switched on. Each delivery you finish should create a waiting group message, including its photo, in the local test database. I can check that it arrived once you've done one.

If the camera opens but saving the photo fails, the app on your phone was built without this version of the file module. In that case it needs one rebuild through EAS.

Still left outside the app: setting up the relay on the VPS, and deploying the engine with its secret. I'll deploy once you tell me to commit and deploy.

content.text:
It's now one photo per item: all of an item's packs together in one shot, and each photo becomes its own group message. Both backends pass the end-to-end check and the app builds. I still haven't seen the camera on a phone, and nothing is committed or deployed.

**On the phone**
- **Receive:** under the amount there's a "Photo of these packs" card with a hint like "Put all 50 packets together and take one photo. It goes to the office group." The main button reads **Take photo** and opens the camera. Once the photo is in, the button changes to **Add to delivery**.
- **Delivery list:** no photo step any more. Each item shows its own photo as its picture, and **Finish** saves straight away.
- **Flag and continue:** uses the item's photo if one was taken. Otherwise it opens the camera first.
- **Same item scanned again:** each scan keeps its own photo, so that item gets two messages.
- **Leaving without adding:** removing an item, cancelling the delivery, or backing out of Receive deletes the unused photo from the phone.

**In the group**, one message per item, with its photo:
> 📦 *Received*: *Milk*
> 50 l (30 l exp 20 Oct 2026, 20 l exp 25 Oct 2026)
> 👤 Sana · 🕓 4:31 pm, 9 Oct
> #received #milk

The "50 l" is because I recorded 50 one-litre packs in the test. With your real items it reads the item's own pack count.

A message waits until every dated batch in its photo has synced, even if the photo arrives first. Uploads with no item attached, or that aren't an image, are rejected with a plain reason.

**Changed underneath**
- **Server:** photos are now stored per item (engine schema and port migration 0013, both updated) and upload to `/api/inventory/receipts/photo`.
- **App:** photos travel in a new sync queue entry, `item_photo`.
- **Local data:** I dropped the old one-photo-per-delivery table from the local test database only. It never existed anywhere else.
- **WhatsApp agent:** nothing changed. It posts whatever the server queues.

To try it, shake the phone and tap **Reload**, then receive an item: take its photo, add it, and tap **Finish**. Your phone talks to the local engine, so I can confirm the per-item message was queued once you've done one.

#!/bin/bash
# Office-flow local test: OpenWA gateway + WhatsApp agent (with the ops relay).
# Everything they write (WhatsApp login, databases, Chrome profile, archive,
# photos, logs) stays inside this folder. ./cleanup.sh removes all of it.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
OPENWA=/Users/appointy/work/OpenWA
NODE="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v22.22.3/installation/bin/node"

ENGINE_URL="${ENGINE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:4112}"   # local office-ops-engine
RELAY_SECRET="${RELAY_SECRET:-relay-test-secret}"   # must match the engine's OPS_RELAY_SECRET
GROUP="${GROUP:-Office-flow}"                       # WhatsApp group the messages go to

mkdir -p "$HERE/gateway" "$HERE/agent/archive" "$HERE/logs"

running() { [ -f "$1" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$1")" 2>/dev/null; }

# 1. OpenWA gateway: localhost only, working folder = ./gateway (its ./data
#    holds the WhatsApp login, SQLite files, media and the Chrome profile).
if running "$HERE/gateway.pid"; then
  echo "gateway already running"
else
  (
    cd "$HERE/gateway"
    env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
      HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=2785 LOG_LEVEL=warn \
      DATABASE_NAME=./data/openwa.sqlite SESSION_DATA_PATH=./data/sessions STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH=./data/media \
      nohup "$NODE" "$OPENWA/dist/main.js" >> "$HERE/logs/gateway.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$HERE/gateway.pid"
  )
  echo -n "starting gateway"
  for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:2785/api/health 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200 && break
    echo -n "."; sleep 1
  done
  echo
fi

# 2. WhatsApp agent: archive + photos in ./agent, bot replies off, no Google
#    Drive (nothing leaves this laptop except the WhatsApp posts).
if running "$HERE/agent.pid"; then
  echo "agent already running"
else
  [ -f "$HERE/agent/bot-off.json" ] || echo '{ "enabled": false, "trigger": "bot", "requireTrigger": true, "rules": [] }' > "$HERE/agent/bot-off.json"
  (
    cd "$OPENWA/apps/whatsapp-agent"
    env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
      ARCHIVE_DIR="$HERE/agent/archive" BOT_CONFIG="$HERE/agent/bot-off.json" AGENT_CLI=0 \
      ARCHIVER_PORT=4100 OPENWA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:2785 OPENWA_API_KEY=dev-admin-key \
      OPS_RELAY_URL="$ENGINE_URL" OPS_RELAY_SECRET="$RELAY_SECRET" OPS_GROUP="$GROUP" OPS_RELAY_INTERVAL_MS=15000 \
      nohup "$NODE" server.mjs >> "$HERE/logs/agent.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$HERE/agent.pid"
  )
  sleep 2
fi

echo
echo "Open http://127.0.0.1:4100 and link WhatsApp (Linked devices > Link a device)."
echo "Messages go to the group \"$GROUP\". Logs: $HERE/logs/"
echo "Stop: ./stop.sh    Remove everything: ./cleanup.sh"

# Office-flow local test: OpenWA gateway + WhatsApp agent (with the ops relay).

set -euo pipefail

OPENWA=/Users/appointy/work/OpenWA
NODE="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v22.22.3/installation/bin/node"

ENGINE_URL="${ENGINE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:4112}"   # local office-ops-engine
RELAY_SECRET="${RELAY_SECRET:-relay-test-secret}"   # must match the engine's OPS_RELAY_SECRET
GROUP="${GROUP:-Office-flow}"                       # WhatsApp group the messages go to

mkdir -p "$HERE/gateway" "$HERE/agent/archive" "$HERE/logs"

running() { [ -f "$1" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$1")" 2>/dev/null; }

# 1. OpenWA gateway: localhost only, working folder = ./gateway (its ./data
#    holds the WhatsApp login, SQLite files, media and the Chrome profile).
if running "$HERE/gateway.pid"; then
  echo "gateway already running"
else
  (
    cd "$HERE/gateway"
    env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
      HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=2785 LOG_LEVEL=warn \
      DATABASE_NAME=./data/openwa.sqlite SESSION_DATA_PATH=./data/sessions STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH=./data/media \
      nohup "$NODE" "$OPENWA/dist/main.js" >> "$HERE/logs/gateway.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$HERE/gateway.pid"
  )
  echo -n "starting gateway"
  for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:2785/api/health 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200 && break
    echo -n "."; sleep 1
  done
  echo
fi

#    Drive (nothing leaves this laptop except the WhatsApp posts).
if running "$HERE/agent.pid"; then

else

fi

WhatsApp is ready to link. Gateway and agent are running from `/Users/appointy/work/office-flow-test` and listen only on this laptop, not the office network.

**Your steps:**
1. **Create the group.** On your phone, make a WhatsApp group named **Office-flow**. It must include the number you're about to link. Any upper or lower case works, but the spelling must match.
2. **Link the laptop.** Open **http://127.0.0.1:4100** in your browser. On your phone go to WhatsApp > Settings > **Linked devices** > **Link a device** and scan the QR on that page. The code refreshes every ~20 seconds, so scan the newest one. Yes, WhatsApp allows up to 4 linked devices, and this takes one.
3. **Receive one item in the field app.** Shake the phone and tap **Reload**, sign in, then: Receive > scan or pick an item > take the photo of all its packs > **Add to delivery** > **Finish**.

Within about 15 seconds of the photo uploading, a "📦 Received" message with the photo should appear in **Office-flow**. A count correction that changes the number should post too.

**How this test is set up:**
- **Messages come from your own number,** since that's the account you're linking. The dedicated SIM is for the real VPS setup later.
- **The bot's auto-replies are switched off,** so it won't answer anything in your chats.
- **Google Drive is off.** Posted photos are filed only in the test folder.
- **The daily take-out summary goes out after 6 pm.**
- **My leftover test messages are cleared,** so the group only gets what you do now.

**When you're done**, run these in `/Users/appointy/work/office-flow-test`:
- `./stop.sh` pauses everything and keeps the WhatsApp link.
- `./start.sh` resumes without a new scan.
- `./cleanup.sh` ends the experiment. It asks for "yes", unlinks the laptop from your WhatsApp, stops both services and deletes the whole folder: the login, databases, the Chrome profile WhatsApp Web runs in, photos and logs.

Two things the clean-up doesn't remove:
- the Chrome download in `~/.cache/puppeteer` (525 MB), which was already there before this test and is shared with the OpenWA repo;
- the local test database and engine, which live in the system temp folder.

Tell me once you've scanned and I'll check the link and that the relay found the group.

content.text:
The fallback works: listing groups no longer errors. WhatsApp currently reports your number in **no groups**. That's expected if the laptop hasn't synced your chat list yet; a freshly linked device often hasn't. A group created now arrives on the laptop live.

So go ahead:

1. **Create the group.** On your phone, create a group named **Office-flow** and add at least one other person (WhatsApp needs one member to create a group).
2. **Say something in it,** for example "test", so the laptop picks up the new chat right away.
3. **Tell me once it exists.** I'll confirm the relay found it. The log will say "posting … to Office-flow" with no "no WhatsApp group named" warning.

Then receive one item in the field app (photo of all its packs > **Add to delivery** > **Finish**), and the "📦 Received" message with the photo should land in Office-flow within about 15 seconds.

What I changed on the way:
- **Group listing:** your WhatsApp's chat list broke the standard group lookup, so the gateway now falls back to reading just the group names and ids. This change is in the OpenWA repo.
- **Error wording:** the relay now says "WhatsApp could not list its groups" instead of the misleading "cannot reach the engine".
- **Restarts:** `start.sh` now reconnects the saved WhatsApp login after a restart, with no new QR.

content.text:
It posted. Your Bisleri Water item from the field app should now be in **Office-flow** as a photo with its "📦 *Received*" caption. It was sent at 4:54 pm with archive reference `WA-261009-12R34G`, and the engine dropped its copy of the photo afterwards.

**Why it took several fixes:**
1. **Photo too large for the gateway:** OpenWA accepted at most 100 KB per request, and your photo was 1.1 MB. It now accepts up to 25 MB, adjustable with a `BODY_LIMIT` setting.
2. **WhatsApp Web changed in late September, which broke the photo-sending library.** The library is whatsapp-web.js, OpenWA's link to WhatsApp Web. The change broke photo sends with "Data passed to getter must include an id property" (upstream issue #201921), and it is also why the group list failed earlier. It's fixed upstream but not yet released on npm, so I pinned OpenWA to the fixed commit `064a3d5`. Since then the group list works normally too, and the fallback I added stays only as a safety net.
3. **Marking the chat as read:** sends no longer mark the chat as read first, which could also trigger that error.

**Changed in the OpenWA repo, all uncommitted:**
- the whatsapp-web.js pin in `package.json`, plus the lock file;
- the opt-in `HOST` setting;
- the 25 MB upload limit;
- the group-list fallback;
- sends no longer marking chats as read;
- the relay's clearer error wording.

**Please check the group:**
- Did the photo message arrive, and does the caption look right?
- An earlier test line, "Office-flow test: relay connected", may also be there. That was me checking that text sends work.

**Next things to try:**
- Receive a couple more items, including one with two expiry dates.
- Correct a count to a different number; that posts a ✏️ message.
- After 6 pm, the take-out summary goes out if you took anything out today.

content.text:
The messages are now clean, uniform cards with no emoji or hashtags in the text. I previewed every type locally and posted nothing to your group while doing it. Everything is running again with the new format; receive an item in the app to see it in Office-flow.

**What the group will see**

A received item (with its photo):
```
*Stock received*
Item: Milk
Quantity: 50 l
Batches: 30 l, expiry 20 Oct 2026; 20 l, expiry 25 Oct 2026
Received by: Sana
Time: 9 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm
Ref: RCV-BE9759AB
```
With a single expiry date it shows `Expiry: 1 May 2027` instead of `Batches`. If the count didn't match the order, it adds `Order check: Count does not match the order. Please check.`

A count correction:
```
*Stock count corrected*
Item: Milk
System count: 6 l 400 ml
Shelf count: 2 l 500 ml
Difference: 3 l 900 ml short
Counted by: Sana
Time: 9 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm
Ref: CNT-A3AF68B3
```

Low stock (out of stock follows the same shape, with `In stock: None`):
```
*Low stock*
Item: Milk
In stock: 2 l 500 ml
Reorder level: 3 l
Action: Reorder
Time: 9 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm
Ref: LOW-34B31CC1
```

Daily summary, after 6 pm:
```
*Daily take out summary*
Date: 9 Oct 2026
Total take outs: 4
Items:
1. Sugar: 1 kg (4 times)
Taken by: Sana (4)
Ref: SUM-…
```

The Milk numbers in these previews come from my test data, which is why the actual cards showed odd totals like 152 l. Your real items will show their own amounts.

**How a future AI agent can read the group**
- **Titles never change,** so the first line tells it the kind: Stock received, Stock count corrected, Low stock, Out of stock, Daily take out summary.
- **Every fact is a `Label: value` line** with a fixed label set: Item, Quantity, Expiry, Batches, System count, Shelf count, Difference, In stock, Reorder level, Received by, Counted by, Time, Ref. Lists are `Items:` followed by numbered lines.
- **Dates and times always look the same,** in office time: "9 Oct 2026, 5:00 pm".
- **The `Ref:` line gives each message a unique id.** Its prefix is the type (RCV, CNT, LOW, OOS, SUM), so the agent can count, link and cite messages, and a person can quote one.

**Search tags** such as `received` and `milk` no longer appear in the text. The agent still stores them with each post in its archive, and in the Drive file name once Drive is connected, so search keeps working.

The same change is in the engine and the Supabase port, and both compile.

name: Deploy

# Runs on the office server itself through a self-hosted runner, which connects
# out to GitHub; the server needs no port open to the internet.
# Setup: deploy/README.md
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Documentation changes don't need a restart.
    paths-ignore: ['**.md', 'docs/**']
  workflow_dispatch:

# One deploy at a time; a newer push waits for the running one instead of cancelling it mid-restart.
concurrency:
  group: deploy-office
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, whatsapp-agent]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Deploy ${{ github.sha }}
        # DEPLOY_DIR: the checkout the service runs from (repository variable).
        env:
          DEPLOY_DIR: ${{ vars.DEPLOY_DIR }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$DEPLOY_DIR" ]; then
            echo "::error::Set the DEPLOY_DIR repository variable to the server's checkout (see deploy/README.md)"
            exit 1
          fi
          "$DEPLOY_DIR/deploy/deploy.sh" "${{ github.sha }}"
# Deploying to the office server

Push to `main` and the office PC updates itself: it pulls the commit, rebuilds, restarts the service and checks it came back up. If the new version doesn't come up healthy, it goes back to the previous one. A deploy takes about a minute and a half.

```
git push (main) ──► GitHub ──► self-hosted runner on the office PC ──► deploy/deploy.sh
                                (it connects out to GitHub, so the PC
                                 needs no port open to the internet)
```

Set up on 2026-09-29. Before that, the agent ran by hand in a `tmux` session on the same PC.

## What is installed where

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Office PC | Arch Linux, `10.0.0.18`, office network only. Log in with `ssh appointy@10.0.0.18` |
| Checkout the service runs from | `/home/appointy/git/whatsapp-agent` (GitHub variable `DEPLOY_DIR` points here) |
| App service | systemd **user** service `whatsapp-agent`, unit at `~/.config/systemd/user/whatsapp-agent.service` (written by `deploy/install-service.sh`) |
| GitHub runner | `/home/appointy/actions-runner`, system service `actions.runner.junaid-appointy-whatsapp-agent.appointy`, runner name `appointy`, label `whatsapp-agent` |
| Node | fnm, used through its `default` alias: `/home/appointy/.local/share/fnm/aliases/default/bin` |
| Ports (local only) | OpenWA API `127.0.0.1:2785`, agent page `127.0.0.1:4100` |
| State kept across deploys | `.env` files, `data/` (WhatsApp login, OpenWA database), `apps/whatsapp-agent/archive/` (messages, Drive connection, upload ledger) |

| File in this repo | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` | On every push to `main` (and **Actions → Deploy → Run workflow**), runs `deploy.sh` on the runner labelled `whatsapp-agent`. Pushes that only change `*.md` or `docs/` skip it |
| `deploy/deploy.sh [sha]` | Fetch, `git reset --hard` to the commit, `npm ci`, build, restart, health check, roll back on failure |
| `deploy/install-service.sh` | One-time: writes the systemd unit, enables lingering, builds and starts the service. `--unit-only` just rewrites the unit, which every deploy does |
| `scripts/whatsapp-agent.mjs` | What the service runs (`npm run whatsapp-agent`): OpenWA + the agent together. `OPENWA_MODE=prod` (set by the unit) runs the built OpenWA from `dist/` |

## How a deploy works

1. A push to `main` queues the **Deploy** workflow. Only one deploy runs at a time; a newer push waits for the current one instead of cancelling it mid-restart.
2. The runner on the office PC picks it up and runs `$DEPLOY_DIR/deploy/deploy.sh <pushed sha>`.
3. `deploy.sh` fetches and runs `git reset --hard <sha>`, then **runs itself again from the new commit**, so changes to the deploy script apply in the same deploy.
4. It runs `npm ci` (root and `apps/whatsapp-agent`) and `npm run build`.
   - **The build fails:** the running service is not touched, the checkout goes back to the previous commit, and the job fails.
5. It runs `systemctl --user restart whatsapp-agent` and polls `http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/status` for up to 120 s. Healthy means the agent is up and can reach OpenWA; WhatsApp being linked is not required.
   - **It doesn't become healthy:** it prints the last 40 log lines, rebuilds and restarts the previous commit, and the job fails.

WhatsApp and Drive stay connected across deploys: the WhatsApp login lives in `data/` and the Drive connection in `archive/`, both git-ignored. After a restart WhatsApp reconnects by itself within about a minute.

## Decisions, and why

- **Self-hosted runner, not SSH from GitHub.** The PC is only reachable on the office network, so GitHub's cloud runners can't SSH in. The runner connects out to GitHub, so no port or VPN is needed. It's safe to run here because the repo is private: only people with push access can run code on the PC.
- **A runner rather than a timer that polls git.** A timer would work too, but the runner shows every deploy, its log and its result in the Actions tab, and deploys can be started or re-run from there.
- **The same `deploy.sh` by hand.** If GitHub or the runner is down, `deploy/deploy.sh` over SSH does exactly what the pipeline does.
- **systemd user service with lingering.** It restarts on crash, starts at boot, and keeps running without anyone logged in, all without running the app as root. `KillMode=control-group` stops OpenWA, the agent and WhatsApp's Chrome together.
- **The service stops with SIGINT, like Ctrl+C.** `concurrently` treats only SIGINT as a clean stop. With systemd's default SIGTERM, OpenWA exits with an error during shutdown (a harmless Nest database-module error), `concurrently` restarts it mid-stop, and after 30 s systemd kills everything, WhatsApp's browser included. That left the next start stuck at "Linking…" (found 2026-09-29).
- **The unit is rewritten on every deploy.** `deploy.sh` runs `install-service.sh --unit-only` before restarting, so changes to the service definition deploy like code.
- **Built OpenWA in production (`OPENWA_MODE=prod`).** The default `nest start --watch` recompiles and restarts on every file change, which would restart OpenWA partway through `git reset` and `npm ci`.
- **`git reset --hard`, not `git pull`.** The server always matches the pushed commit exactly and can't get stuck on merge conflicts. **Edits made on the server are lost on the next deploy**, so change code by pushing. When this was set up, the server had `sqlite3` added to `apps/whatsapp-agent/package.json` by hand; nothing in the agent uses it (OpenWA has its own `sqlite3`), so it was dropped.
- **Deploys don't wait for CI.** The CI workflow's lint and format checks were already failing on existing code, and gating on them would block every deploy. The rollback health check is the safety net instead. If CI is made green, the deploy job can be made to wait for it.
- **Health check rather than "linked to WhatsApp".** Linking depends on the phone and on WhatsApp's servers; a deploy shouldn't roll back because the phone is offline.
- **Node through fnm's `default` alias.** fnm puts `node` on `PATH` through `/run/user/<uid>/fnm_multishells/<id>`, a folder that exists only for one login shell and is gone after a reboot. The service and `deploy.sh` use `~/.local/share/fnm/aliases/default/bin` instead, which follows `fnm default`.
- **Higher OpenWA rate limits under the launcher.** OpenWA allows 1000 requests an hour by default, and the agent polling for a QR scan used that up in about 15 minutes, after which it wrongly showed WhatsApp as offline. The launcher raises the limits, and the agent polls every 15 s once linked. OpenWA also listens on the office network (port 2785), but every request still needs its API key.
- **The agent's page stays on `127.0.0.1`.** It has no login of its own, so it's reached through an SSH tunnel rather than opened to the office network.

## Day to day

```sh
ssh appointy@10.0.0.18
systemctl --user status whatsapp-agent          # running?
journalctl --user -u whatsapp-agent -f          # live logs (Ctrl+C stops watching, not the service)
systemctl --user restart whatsapp-agent         # restart by hand
cd ~/git/whatsapp-agent && deploy/deploy.sh     # deploy latest main by hand
deploy/deploy.sh <sha>                          # deploy, or go back to, a specific commit
sudo ~/actions-runner/svc.sh status             # is the GitHub runner up?
```

### The web page, QR code and Google sign-in

From your laptop:

```sh
ssh -L 4100:127.0.0.1:4100 appointy@10.0.0.18
```

then open http://localhost:4100. Google Drive sign-in works through this tunnel too, since its redirect address is `http://localhost:4100`. If WhatsApp needs linking again, the QR code is on that page and in `journalctl --user -u whatsapp-agent -f`.

The terminal commands (`qr`, `drive`, `unlink`…) don't work under the service, which has no terminal. Use the page instead.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy job stays **Queued** | The runner is down: `sudo ~/actions-runner/svc.sh status`, then `sudo ~/actions-runner/svc.sh start` |
| Deploy fails with "Set the DEPLOY_DIR repository variable" | Set it under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables**. Variables are read when a job is queued, so re-run the job after setting it |
| Deploy fails at `npm ci` or the build | Read the job log. The service is still on the previous version |
| Deploy "not healthy", rolled back | The job log shows the last 40 service log lines; more with `journalctl --user -u whatsapp-agent -n 200` |
| `node: not found` after upgrading Node with fnm | `fnm default <version>`, then `deploy/install-service.sh` |
| `tmux` or other tools say "missing or unsuitable terminal: xterm-ghostty" | Your terminal is Ghostty: `export TERM=xterm-256color`, or once from the Mac: `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty \| ssh appointy@10.0.0.18 -- tic -x -` |
| WhatsApp shows "offline" but OpenWA is up | Look for `429 Too Many Requests` in the logs (rate limits, see above) |
| Everything down after a reboot | `systemctl --user status whatsapp-agent`; lingering must be on: `loginctl show-user appointy -p Linger` should say `yes` |

### Re-registering the runner

For example after moving it to another machine. On GitHub go to **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner → Linux x64**, then as `appointy` on the office PC:

```sh
cd ~/actions-runner
sudo ./svc.sh stop && sudo ./svc.sh uninstall
./config.sh remove --token <token from the GitHub page>
./config.sh --url https://github.com/junaid-appointy/whatsapp-agent --token <new token>
#   labels: whatsapp-agent        work folder: press Enter (_work)
sudo ./svc.sh install appointy && sudo ./svc.sh start
```

## Setting it up on another machine

1. Stop any copy running by hand (in `tmux`: `tmux attach`, then Ctrl+C). `ss -ltnp | grep -E ':2785|:4100'` should print nothing.
2. Clone the repo, or update an existing checkout with `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main`. To keep an existing WhatsApp login, use the folder whose `data/` holds it. `git fetch` must work without a password; use SSH with a deploy key if needed.
3. Run `deploy/install-service.sh` as the user that should own the service, not root. It asks for `sudo` once to enable lingering.
4. Install the runner (see above) as the same user, with the label `whatsapp-agent`.
5. Set the repository variable `DEPLOY_DIR` to the checkout's full path.

### Re-registering the runner

For example after moving it to another machine. On GitHub go to **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner → Linux x64**, then as `appointy` on the office PC:

```sh
cd ~/actions-runner
sudo ./svc.sh stop && sudo ./svc.sh uninstall
./config.sh remove --token <token from the GitHub page>
./config.sh --url https://github.com/junaid-appointy/whatsapp-agent --token <new token>
#   labels: whatsapp-agent        work folder: press Enter (_work)
sudo ./svc.sh install appointy && sudo ./svc.sh start
```

## Setting it up on another machine

1. Stop any copy running by hand (in `tmux`: `tmux attach`, then Ctrl+C). `ss -ltnp | grep -E ':2785|:4100'` should print nothing.
2. Clone the repo, or update an existing checkout with `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main`. To keep an existing WhatsApp login, use the folder whose `data/` holds it. `git fetch` must work without a password; use SSH with a deploy key if needed.
3. Run `deploy/install-service.sh` as the user that should own the service, not root. It asks for `sudo` once to enable lingering.
4. Install the runner (see above) as the same user, with the label `whatsapp-agent`.
5. Set the repository variable `DEPLOY_DIR` to the checkout's full path.

aiTitle: Inventory app role-based access and UX improvements

content.text:
Yes, all of it is possible, and most of the pieces already exist on both sides. One correction from the deploy notes: the "VPS" is the office PC (Arch Linux, `10.0.0.18`, office network only). Every push to `main` of `junaid-appointy/whatsapp-agent` redeploys it automatically: a GitHub runner on that PC pulls the commit, rebuilds and restarts the agent, and rolls back if it doesn't come up healthy. So anything we push to `main` is live on the PC about 90 seconds later.

## What exists today

| | WhatsApp agent (office PC) | Office Ops backend (Bifrost) |
|---|---|---|
| Messaging | Receives every incoming message; sends through OpenWA | Has a channel system: incoming messages go to the AI router for classification and extraction; replies go back through the channel |
| AI | Its own bot (Gemini or Claude, trigger word) | Already runs the AI |
| Google Drive | Uploads incoming files; writes monthly message Sheets | Has Google sign-in, but only for Sheets |
| Photos | — | Stores app photos only until they're posted |

## How it would work

```
WhatsApp ⇄ office PC: OpenWA + agent (transport only, no AI, no Drive)
              │  incoming: agent POSTs each message (+ media) to the backend
              │  outgoing: agent asks the backend every 15 s for messages to send
              ▼
     Office Ops backend: AI routing, replies, ops cards, Google Drive storage
              ▲
     Field app: compressed photos, like WhatsApp
```

**1. The agent becomes a pure courier.**
- It forwards each incoming message (text, sender, group, media) to the backend, authenticated with the relay secret.
- If the backend is down, it keeps a local queue and retries, so nothing is lost.
- It sends whatever the backend queues: replies to a specific chat, and the ops cards we built. Today it can only post to one group, so each queued message will carry its target chat.
- The AI bot, the Drive upload and the Sheets code come out of the agent. Its local archive shrinks to a short-lived retry buffer.
- The PC calling out to the backend over the internet is fine: it needs no open port, just like the runner.

**2. The backend handles the brains.**
- A new WhatsApp channel turns forwarded messages into its standard message format and passes them to the existing AI router, the same path Telegram uses today. Replies go into the queue for the agent to send.

**3. Google Drive moves to the backend.**
- One shared storage service saves app photos and incoming WhatsApp media to Drive. It records the Drive link on the receipt or message, so the photo bytes no longer need to sit in the database.
- The admin connects Drive once in the dashboard, which means adding the `drive.file` permission to the existing Google sign-in. Google treats that permission as non-sensitive, so it needs no verification or security review.
- The monthly message Sheets can move over too, using the same method the agent uses today.

**4. App photos processed like WhatsApp.** WhatsApp resizes a photo's long side to about 1,600 px, compresses it to roughly 150–300 KB, and removes hidden data such as GPS location. Your test photo was 1.1 MB.
- The app will do the same before saving, using `expo-image-manipulator`. That needs **one dev app rebuild through EAS**, which is free.
- Uploads then take about a quarter of the data on weak Wi-Fi.
- Optionally the app can show WhatsApp-style status on each photo: clock while waiting, one tick when uploaded, two ticks when posted to the group.

## Cost
- **Monthly: ₹0.** Bifrost, the office PC and Google Workspace Drive storage are already paid for, and there are no per-message fees.
- **One-time:**
  - backend channel plus Drive: about 2–3 days;
  - slimming the agent: about 1 day;
  - app compression plus the rebuild: about half a day.

## Risks before we start
1. **My OpenWA changes are behind `main`.** The relay and the four fixes (25 MB limit, whatsapp-web.js pin, group fallback, no mark-as-read) sit on an older local copy, while `main` has 4 newer commits. Those include about 250 changed lines in the same whatsapp-web.js file I edited. I'll merge onto `main` and test in the `office-flow-test` folder before anything is pushed, because a push deploys immediately.
2. **The backend's AI key is broken.** The Gemini key in the engine's config is rejected by Google. Once the AI lives only in the backend, replies need a working key there; the agent's current key could be moved over.
3. **The agent's Drive and Sheets features stop.** Incoming files of the bot number will be saved by the backend instead. What's already in Drive stays where it is.

## Decisions I need from you
1. **Which chats go to the backend?** Every chat of the bot number (simple, since it's a dedicated SIM), or only listed groups?
2. **Whose Drive?** An admin's own Drive (simplest), or a **Shared Drive**, so files don't belong to one person who might leave? I recommend the Shared Drive.
3. **What should the backend do with incoming WhatsApp messages at first?**
   - just save them (Drive plus a searchable log); or
   - also run them through the AI router, so it can understand requests like "2 boxes of pens received" or "visitor coming at 3" and reply.
4. **WhatsApp-style ticks on app photos:** include them now, or later?

p='lib/postgres-schema.ts'
s=open(p).read()
old="""    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_inv_receipt_photos_receipts
      ON inventory_receipt_photos USING GIN (receipt_ids);
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old, old+"""    -- Where the photo lives in the org's Shared Drive (lib/google-drive.ts).
    -- The bytes above are dropped once the photo is both posted and in Drive.
    ALTER TABLE inventory_receipt_photos ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS drive_file_id TEXT;
    ALTER TABLE inventory_receipt_photos ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS drive_link TEXT;
    ALTER TABLE inventory_receipt_photos ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS drive_error TEXT;

    -- Every WhatsApp message the office number receives (forwarded by the
    -- agent on the office PC, which keeps no copy). Searchable log; media
    -- goes to the Shared Drive and media_bytes is held only until it is there.
    -- wa_id is the agent's stable message id, so a re-forward is a no-op.
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_messages (
      wa_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      session_id TEXT,
      chat_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      chat_name TEXT,
      is_group BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      sender_id TEXT,
      sender_name TEXT,
      from_me BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      type TEXT NOT NULL,
      body TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
      quoted_body TEXT,
      sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
      media_mime TEXT,
      media_filename TEXT,
      media_size INTEGER,
      media_bytes BYTEA,
      drive_file_id TEXT,
      drive_link TEXT,
      drive_error TEXT,
      bot_invoked BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      search tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
        to_tsvector('simple',
          coalesce(body, '') || ' ' || coalesce(sender_name, '') || ' ' ||
          coalesce(chat_name, '') || ' ' || coalesce(media_filename, ''))
      ) STORED
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_search ON wa_messages USING GIN (search);
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_chat ON wa_messages(chat_id, sent_at DESC);
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_sent ON wa_messages(sent_at DESC);
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_drive_pending
      ON wa_messages(created_at) WHERE media_bytes IS NOT NULL AND drive_file_id IS NULL;
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

input.content:
# WhatsApp Agent

The office WhatsApp number's courier to the **Office Ops backend**. It does two things and keeps nothing:

- **Incoming:** every message the number receives, in every chat (text, photos, videos, voice notes, documents), is forwarded to the backend. The backend saves it in a searchable log, puts the media in the org's Google Shared Drive, and decides what to do with it (it only involves the AI when a message starts with `bot` or tags the number).
- **Outgoing:** whatever the backend queues is sent: ops cards in the ops group (item photos, count corrections, low stock, the daily summary) and replies in any chat.

There is no AI, no Google Drive and no message archive in the agent any more; all of that lives in the backend.

```
WhatsApp ⇄ OpenWA (this machine) ⇄ agent ──► backend   POST /api/ops-relay/inbound   (each incoming message)
                                         ◄── backend   POST /api/ops-relay/claim      (what to send, every 15 s)
```

Both directions are calls **out** from this machine to the backend with one shared secret, so it needs no open port, and OpenWA's admin key never leaves it.

## Nothing is lost

- **Backend down or no internet:** each incoming message is written to `archive/queue/` first and deleted only after the backend confirms it. Waiting messages go out oldest first when the backend is back (retry with backoff up to 5 minutes). A message the backend refuses outright is moved to `archive/queue/refused/` instead of blocking the rest.
- **WhatsApp down or this machine off:** outgoing messages wait in the backend. A message the agent took but never confirmed is handed out again after a few minutes.

## Setup

Needs **Node 22 LTS**.

```bash
npm install
cp apps/whatsapp-agent/.env.example apps/whatsapp-agent/.env   # then fill it in
npm run whatsapp-agent
```

`.env` needs `OPS_RELAY_URL` (the backend), `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` (the same value as the backend's `OPS_RELAY_SECRET`) and `OPS_GROUP` (the ops group's name, or its `…@g.us` id). See `.env.example`.

Link WhatsApp once: the QR code is printed in the terminal and shown at http://localhost:4100 (WhatsApp > Settings > Linked devices > Link a device). A saved login reconnects by itself after restarts. On the office PC, open the page through an SSH tunnel (see `deploy/README.md`).

Terminal commands (`help`): `status`, `qr` (fresh code), `retry` (send waiting messages now), `unlink`.

## Config

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPS_RELAY_URL` | none | The Office Ops backend |
| `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` | none | Shared secret; must equal the backend's |
| `OPS_GROUP` | none | Group for ops cards (name or `…@g.us` id). Replies need no setting |
| `OPS_RELAY_INTERVAL_MS` | `15000` | How often to ask the backend for messages to send |
| `FORWARD_ONLY` | every chat | Forward only these chats (names or ids, comma-separated), e.g. when testing with a personal number |
| `ARCHIVE_DIR` | `./archive` | State folder: webhook secret and the forwarding queue |
| `ARCHIVER_PORT` / `ARCHIVER_HOST` | `4100` / `127.0.0.1` | The local page. It has no login: keep it on 127.0.0.1 |
| `OPENWA_URL` / `OPENWA_API_KEY` | `http://127.0.0.1:2785` / `dev-admin-key` | OpenWA |
| `WEBHOOK_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/webhook` | URL OpenWA calls (an IP, not `localhost`) |
| `AGENT_CLI` | on | `0` turns off the terminal QR and commands |

## Upgrading from the archiving agent

Earlier versions saved messages locally and to a personal Google Drive, and had an AI auto-reply bot. Those are gone: the backend does it now, in the org's Shared Drive. Files already in that Drive stay there. The old `archive/` contents (per-chat folders, `messages.jsonl`) are left untouched and are no longer read; delete them when you no longer need them. Only `archive/.webhook-secret` and `archive/queue/` are used.

## Limitations

- Messages you send from the phone itself are not forwarded: OpenWA only reports incoming messages.
- whatsapp-web.js drives WhatsApp Web and breaks when WhatsApp changes it. It is pinned to a fixed upstream commit (see the root `package.json`); when sends fail with errors from inside WhatsApp Web, check upstream for a newer fix.

# WhatsApp Agent

The office WhatsApp number's courier to the **Office Ops backend**. It does two things and keeps nothing:

- **Incoming:** every message the number receives, in every chat (text, photos, videos, voice notes, documents), is forwarded to the backend. The backend saves it in a searchable log, puts the media in the org's Google Shared Drive, and decides what to do with it (it only involves the AI when a message starts with `bot` or tags the number).
- **Outgoing:** whatever the backend queues is sent: ops cards in the ops group (item photos, count corrections, low stock, the daily summary) and replies in any chat.

There is no AI, no Google Drive and no message archive in the agent any more; all of that lives in the backend.

```
WhatsApp ⇄ OpenWA (this machine) ⇄ agent ──► backend   POST /api/ops-relay/inbound   (each incoming message)
                                         ◄── backend   POST /api/ops-relay/claim      (what to send, every 15 s)
```

Both directions are calls **out** from this machine to the backend with one shared secret, so it needs no open port, and OpenWA's admin key never leaves it.

## Nothing is lost

- **Backend down or no internet:** each incoming message is written to `archive/queue/` first and deleted only after the backend confirms it. Waiting messages go out oldest first when the backend is back (retry with backoff up to 5 minutes). A message the backend refuses outright is moved to `archive/queue/refused/` instead of blocking the rest.
- **WhatsApp down or this machine off:** outgoing messages wait in the backend. A message the agent took but never confirmed is handed out again after a few minutes.

## Setup

Needs **Node 22 LTS**.

```bash
npm install
cp apps/whatsapp-agent/.env.example apps/whatsapp-agent/.env   # then fill it in
npm run whatsapp-agent
```

`.env` needs `OPS_RELAY_URL` (the backend), `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` (the same value as the backend's `OPS_RELAY_SECRET`) and `OPS_GROUP` (the ops group's name, or its `…@g.us` id). See `.env.example`.

Link WhatsApp once: the QR code is printed in the terminal and shown at http://localhost:4100 (WhatsApp > Settings > Linked devices > Link a device). A saved login reconnects by itself after restarts. On the office PC, open the page through an SSH tunnel (see `deploy/README.md`).

Terminal commands (`help`): `status`, `qr` (fresh code), `retry` (send waiting messages now), `unlink`.

| `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` | none | Shared secret; must equal the backend's |

| `OPS_RELAY_INTERVAL_MS` | `15000` | How often to ask the backend for messages to send |
| `FORWARD_ONLY` | every chat | Forward only these chats (names or ids, comma-separated), e.g. when testing with a personal number |
| `ARCHIVE_DIR` | `./archive` | State folder: webhook secret and the forwarding queue |
| `ARCHIVER_PORT` / `ARCHIVER_HOST` | `4100` / `127.0.0.1` | The local page. It has no login: keep it on 127.0.0.1 |
| `OPENWA_URL` / `OPENWA_API_KEY` | `http://127.0.0.1:2785` / `dev-admin-key` | OpenWA |
| `WEBHOOK_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/webhook` | URL OpenWA calls (an IP, not `localhost`) |

-- One Google Drive per archiver. Switching to a different Google account only affects new files; ones already uploaded stay in the old Drive (their local copies are gone).
-- The UI has no login of its own, so keep it on `127.0.0.1` (the default) or put it behind auth before exposing it. Anyone who can open it can unlink WhatsApp or connect a Drive.

content.text:
The code for all of this is built and the local pieces pass their checks. Nothing is committed, pushed or deployed yet. The local test is running, so you can try the WhatsApp side now.

**Built so far**
- **Backend (Node engine)**
  - Every message the agent forwards is saved in a searchable WhatsApp log, and its media goes to the Shared Drive.
  - The AI only runs when a message starts with "bot" or tags the bot's number. Its answer goes back to the same chat as a WhatsApp reply.
  - Item photos also go to the Shared Drive, and the app can ask where each photo is, for its ticks.
  - A new "Read the WhatsApp log" permission controls who can search the log.
- **WhatsApp agent:** rebuilt on top of the latest `main` as a pure courier.
  - Incoming messages are written to disk first and deleted only after the backend confirms them.
  - It sends whatever the backend queues, to the ops group or to a specific chat.
  - It has no AI, no Drive and no archive, just a small status page with the QR code.
  - The deploy notes now say **10.0.0.21**.
- **Field app**
  - Photos are shrunk the way WhatsApp does: long side 1,600 px, JPEG 70%, hidden data stripped. This needs one app rebuild; until then photos upload as they are, without crashing.
  - "Delivery saved" shows live ticks on each item: clock (still on phone), one tick (server has it), two ticks (in the office group).

**Checked locally:** plain messages are saved and duplicates ignored, photo messages wait for Drive (not set up locally), bot calls queue a reply, search finds "pens" from "pen", and the log refuses requests without an admin sign-in. Both apps type-check, the Android bundle builds, and the agent runs and found Office-flow.

**Please try it now in Office-flow.** The test agent forwards only that group, so your personal chats stay out.
1. Send a normal text, for example "2 boxes of pens came today".
2. Send a photo with a caption.
3. Send "bot how many blue pens are left?"

The first two should land in the log, which I'll search to confirm, with no reply in the group. The third should get a reply. Locally it will say "Sorry, I encountered an error…", because no AI key is set on this laptop, but that still shows the bot path works.

**Steps that change real systems, and need your go-ahead**
1. **Shared Drive:** you create a Shared Drive, for example "Office Ops", and add `appointyops@appointy-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com` as **Content manager**. Then send me its link, and I'll set `OPS_SHARED_DRIVE_ID` from it.
2. **App rebuild through EAS (free):** needed for compression. I can start `eas build --profile development --platform android`, or you can.
3. **Move from Neon to Supabase:**
   - Take a read-only `pg_dump` of the Neon database.
   - Check Supabase's scheduled jobs. The experimental Supabase backend left some, and they would run alongside the Node engine's own schedules: duplicate emails, double staff sync. I'd switch those off.
   - Load the Neon data into Supabase's empty `appointy_ops` schema, which replaces the experimental backend's empty tables.
   - Point the engine's `DATABASE_URL` at Supabase's pooler.

   Neon stays untouched as the fallback.
4. **Deploy the engine to Bifrost:** commit, push to `personal`, deploy with `--commit`, plus the new settings `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` and `OPS_SHARED_DRIVE_ID`.
5. **Office PC:** push the agent to `main`, which deploys immediately. Before that, `apps/whatsapp-agent/.env` on the PC needs `OPS_RELAY_URL`, `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` and `OPS_GROUP`, the ops group's name. You can add those over SSH, or let me.

Which of these should I go ahead with? I suggest 3 then 4, then 5 last, once the engine is live.

- **Data copied from Neon:** I backed up Neon read-only to `~/ops-db-backups/neon-appointy_ops-20261014-1108.dump` and loaded it into Supabase. All 94 tables match Neon row for row (6,713 rows). Neon itself is untouched and stays as the fallback.
- **Supabase prepared:** I paused the experimental backend's 6 scheduled jobs so they won't run alongside the engine, and renamed its empty schema to `appointy_ops_port_20261014` instead of deleting it. Both are reversible.
- **Engine settings:** `OPS_RELAY_SECRET` (a random 64-character value) and `OPS_SHARED_DRIVE_ID=0AIq0fmpn24cAUk9PVA` are now in `office-ops-engine/env.updated`, which git ignores.

## Do you have the Supabase URL?
Yes. It's project `tqrmamlqophllikixnuc`, in Mumbai. The engine's new `DATABASE_URL` is the `PROD_DB_SESSION` value in `supabase-backend/.env.prod`. That's the session pooler, which works over IPv4; the direct address is IPv6-only. I won't paste it here because it contains the password, so copy it from that file.

## For you: Google Drive (two clicks)
1. **Turn on the Drive API** for the engine's Google project. Right now Google refuses with "Drive API not enabled": https://console.developers.google.com/apis/api/drive.googleapis.com/overview?project=290964294212 → **Enable**.
2. **Add the service account to the Shared Drive:** open the Shared Drive → **Manage members** → add `appointyops@appointy-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com` as **Content manager**.

Tell me when both are done and I'll re-check access.

## Where the settings go on Bifrost
The engine's settings live on the `ops-engine` service in project `auxilio-v2`, environment `dev`. Three keys change:
- `DATABASE_URL`: the Supabase `PROD_DB_SESSION` value
- `OPS_RELAY_SECRET`: the value in `env.updated`
- `OPS_SHARED_DRIVE_ID`: `0AIq0fmpn24cAUk9PVA`

You can add them in the Bifrost dashboard (auxilio-v2 → dev → ops-engine → environment variables), or let me do it with the CLI. The CLI's login has expired, so run this here first:
```
! bifrost auth login
```
Then I'll do the switch in this order:
1. Re-copy Neon into Supabase (about a minute), so nothing written since this morning's copy is lost.
2. Set the three keys.
3. Commit and push the engine, then deploy with `--commit`.
4. Check that it's healthy.

## For you: the office PC (10.0.0.21)
```
ssh appointy@10.0.0.21
cd ~/git/whatsapp-agent/apps/whatsapp-agent
nano .env
```
Add these three lines, then save:
```
OPS_RELAY_URL=https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site
OPS_RELAY_SECRET=<same value as in office-ops-engine/env.updated>
OPS_GROUP=<the ops group's name exactly as WhatsApp shows it>
```
- To see the secret on your Mac: `grep OPS_RELAY_SECRET office-ops-engine/env.updated`.
- `OPS_GROUP` must be a group the **office number** is in, for example a new "Office Ops" group with the managers. It is not your test group.
- `.env` survives deploys. The current agent ignores these lines, so adding them now is safe. They take effect when the new courier agent is pushed to `main`, and I'll do that last, after the engine is live.

content.text:
Yes, unfortunately. `cat > .env` empties the file the moment you press Enter, before you type anything, so pressing Ctrl+C left `.env` **empty**. Whatever it held is gone. On the current agent that was most likely the Google sign-in client (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`) and an AI key.

It's not urgent, as long as nothing restarts the agent:
- **The running agent still has the old values in memory.** It only reads `.env` when it starts, so it keeps working until the next restart or deploy.
- **The Drive connection itself isn't in `.env`.** It's saved in `archive/`, which wasn't touched.
- **The new courier agent doesn't need any of the lost values.** It has no Drive and no AI. It needs only the three new lines, so nothing has to be recovered unless the old agent restarts first.

Check what's there now. Your last command had a stray `]`; this is the corrected version:
```
ls -la .env
cat .env
```

Then write the three lines. `nano .env` is the safest way. If you'd rather paste, this heredoc writes the whole file in one go:
```
cat > .env <<'EOF'
OPS_RELAY_URL=https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site
OPS_RELAY_SECRET=<value from office-ops-engine/env.updated>
OPS_GROUP=<the ops group's name>
EOF
```

**Don't restart** `whatsapp-agent` on the PC until the courier is deployed. If the old agent restarts with only these lines, it loses its Drive and AI settings in the meantime.

**Where I am:**
- **Done:** Telegram is out of the engine's server, logger, Jira tool and cafeteria.
- **Done:** the WhatsApp group settings backend. Groups stay off until an admin turns them on, private chats have one switch, ops cards go to the groups an admin picks, and there are endpoints for the agent and the dashboard.
- **Still to do:**
  - Switch the six places that sent Telegram alerts (automations, visitor arrival alerts) to the WhatsApp office number. Until then the engine doesn't compile, but nothing is deployed, so nothing is affected.
  - Have the agent fetch the group settings and report its groups.
  - Build the dashboard WhatsApp page.

Google still says Drive is off for project **290964294212** (`appointy-ops`), so that one still needs enabling.

content.text:
The deployed agent only reads secrets from `.env` for two features:

| Setting | Used for |
|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google sign-in for the Drive upload and the monthly message Sheets |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) | The AI auto-reply bot |

Everything else it reads has a built-in default, and is normally left unset: ports, OpenWA address, Drive folder name and the like. The service's own settings, such as `OPENWA_MODE=prod` and the rate limits, live in the systemd unit and the launcher script, not in this `.env`. So they weren't touched.

**Your Mac has a copy with exactly those three names:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (in `OpenWA/apps/whatsapp-agent/.env`). That's almost certainly what the PC's file held. To restore it, run this from your Mac:
```
scp ~/work/OpenWA/apps/whatsapp-agent/.env appointy@10.0.0.21:~/git/whatsapp-agent/apps/whatsapp-agent/.env
```
Then on the PC, add the three new lines to the end, without replacing the file this time:
```
cat >> .env <<'EOF'
OPS_RELAY_URL=https://ops-engine-dev-330299.bifrost.saastack.site
OPS_RELAY_SECRET=<value from office-ops-engine/env.updated>
OPS_GROUP=<the ops group's name>
EOF
```
`>>` adds to the file. A single `>` replaces it, which is what emptied it.

That keeps the current agent fully working if it restarts before we switch to the courier. One caveat: if the PC had been set up with a different Google sign-in client than your Mac, Drive would need re-connecting from the agent's page. After the courier is deployed, the Google and Gemini lines stop mattering, and only the three `OPS_` lines are used.

content.text:
It's a new setting, added by this work, so the old agent ignores it. It tells the agent **which WhatsApp group to post the ops cards in**: stock received (with its photo), count corrected, low or out of stock, and the daily take out summary. You write the group's name exactly as WhatsApp shows it (any upper or lower case), or its `…@g.us` id. The office number has to be a member of that group.

It only affects cards. Replies to someone who wrote "bot …" go back to their own chat and don't use it. Incoming messages don't use it either.

**With the dashboard settings I'm building now, it becomes optional.** An admin will pick, per card type, which groups get it (for example stock received to "Store team", low stock to "Managers"). `OPS_GROUP` is then only a fallback for card types where no group has been picked in the dashboard.

**So you can leave it out.** If it's unset and no group is picked in the dashboard, the cards wait in the backend and nothing is posted. They go out once a group is chosen, unless they're more than a day old, which gets them skipped (photos keep for a week). Setting it now just means cards have somewhere to go from day one, before anyone opens the new dashboard page.
